questions.text:
Consider two files systems A and B , that use contiguous allocation and linked allocation, respectively. A file of size 100 blocks is already stored in A and also in
B. Now, consider inserting a new block in the middle of the file (between [latex]50^{th}  \text{ and }51^{st}[/latex] block), whose data is already available in the memory. Assume that there are enough free blocks at the end of the file and that the file control blocks are already in memory. Let the number of disk accesses required to insert a block in the middle of the file in   A   and     B   are [latex]n_A[/latex] and [latex]n_B[/latex],   respectively, then the value of  [latex]n_A+n_B[/latex]  is
questions.solution:
Contiguous (A): blocks 51-100 must each move one place: read + write for 50 blocks = 100 accesses, plus writing the new block = 1. [latex]n_A=101[/latex].

Linked (B): follow pointers to reach block 50 = 50 reads; write the new block (pointing to block 51) = 1; rewrite block 50's pointer = 1. [latex]n_B=52[/latex].

[latex]n_A+n_B=101+52=153[/latex]

Answer: 153

questions.text: Consider four processes P, Q, R, and S scheduled on a CPU as per round robin algorithm with a time quantum of 4 units. The processes arrive in the order P, Q, R, S, all at time t = 0. There is exactly one context switch from S to Q, exactly one context switch from R to Q, and exactly two context switches from Q to R. There is no context switch from S to P. Switching to a ready process after the termination of another process is also considered a context switch. Which one of the following is NOT possible as CPU burst time (in time units) of these processes?
questions.solution:
Simulate round robin (quantum 4, order P, Q, R, S) for option 4: P = 3, Q = 7, R = 7, S = 3.
- P runs 3 and finishes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q runs 4 (3 left) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R runs 4 (3 left) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S runs 3 and finishes
- [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q runs 3 and finishes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R runs 3 and finishes

Switches: P[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]Q, Q[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]R, R[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]S, S[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]Q, Q[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]R. There is no R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q switch, but exactly one is required. So these burst times are impossible.

(Simulating the other three options gives exactly one S[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]Q, one R[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]Q, two Q[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]R and no S[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]P.)

Answer: P = 3, Q = 7, R = 7, S = 3

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?
questions.solution:
Check each statement (we need the FALSE one):
- The TLB is associative memory and compares all entries in parallel [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- A TLB hit means the page is in main memory, so on a cache miss the word is surely in main memory [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Inverted page table: the frame is found by searching (or hashing and following a chain), so the time depends on the address [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- In a hashed page table, colliding addresses sit on the same chain at different positions, so their access times differ [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Option 3 is FALSE

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: The TLB performs an associative search in parallel on all its valid entries using page number of incoming virtual address.
If the virtual address of a word given by CPU has a TLB hit, but the subsequent search for the word results in a cache miss, then the word will always be present in the main memory.
The memory access time using a given inverted page table is always same for all incoming virtual addresses.
In a system that uses hashed page tables, if two distinct virtual addresses V1 and V2 map to the same value while hashing, then the memory access time of these addresses will not be the same.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are TRUE with respect to deadlocks?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Circular wait is one of the four necessary conditions (with mutual exclusion, hold [latex]\&[/latex] wait, no preemption) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- With multiple instances per resource, a cycle is necessary but not sufficient for deadlock [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- An unsafe state only may lead to deadlock; processes might release resources early [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- If every edge is an assignment edge, no process is waiting for anything, so there is no deadlock [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Options 1 and 4

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Circular wait is a necessary condition for the formation of deadlock.
In a system where each resource has more than one instance, a cycle in its wait-for graph indicates the presence of a deadlock.
If the current allocation of resources to processes leads the system to unsafe state, then deadlock will necessarily occur.
In the resource-allocation graph of a system, if every edge is an assignment edge, then the system is not in deadlock state.

questions.text:
Consider the following threads, [latex]T_1, T_2, \text{ and }T_3[/latex] executing on a single processor, synchronized using three binary semaphore variables, [latex]S_1, S_2, \text{ and }S_3[/latex], operated upon using standard [latex]wait()[/latex] and [latex]signal()[/latex]. The threads can be context switched in any order and at any time.

Which initialization of the semaphores would print the sequence BCABCABCA ...?
questions.solution:
From the code: T2 prints B (needs [latex]S_1[/latex], then signals [latex]S_3[/latex]), T1 prints C (needs [latex]S_3[/latex], signals [latex]S_2[/latex]), T3 prints A (needs [latex]S_2[/latex], signals [latex]S_1[/latex]).

The output must start with B, so only T2 may run first: [latex]S_1=1[/latex] and [latex]S_2=S_3=0[/latex]. Then the chain B [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] C [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] A [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B [latex]\ldots[/latex] repeats forever.

(If [latex]S_2[/latex] or [latex]S_3[/latex] were 1, A or C could be printed first.)

Answer: [latex]S_1=1;\ S_2=0;\ S_3=0[/latex]
